title: From Hourly to Annual: How to Calculate Your Pay, Including Casual Loading, Super, and Salary Sacrifice Airport Lounge Membership
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week formula. Includes casual loading, super on top, and salary sacrifice airport lounge membership considerat
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52, with superannuation paid on top of that amount.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my hourly to annual conversion?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of your base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave and other entitlements. When converting to annual pay, you should first apply the loading to your base rate, then multiply by hours per week and 52 weeks. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 with casual loading. If you work 38 hours per week, your annual gross would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80, before super and tax.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The Super Guarantee requires your employer to contribute 12% of your ordinary time earnings into a super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if your annual gross salary is $80,000, your employer pays an additional $9,600 in super, making your total remuneration $89,600. Super is not deducted from your hourly rate; it is an extra cost for the employer.

faqs.q: Can I salary sacrifice an airport lounge membership, and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Yes, many employers allow salary sacrifice for benefits like airport lounge membership. Under a salary sacrifice arrangement, you agree to forgo part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for a benefit. This reduces your taxable income, potentially lowering your tax and Medicare levy. However, it may also reduce your ordinary time earnings for super guarantee purposes, depending on the type of sacrifice. For example, if you sacrifice $2,000 per year for an airport lounge membership, your taxable income drops by $2,000, but your employer's super obligation may also decrease if the sacrifice is not classified as ordinary earnings. Always check with your employer or the ATO for your specific situation.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward when you know the formula. Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks in a year. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This gives you your gross annual pay before tax, super, and any deductions.

For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours each week, your annual gross is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. Use our [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual equivalent instantly.

Many Australians are paid fortnightly rather than weekly. To find your fortnightly gross, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same $30 per hour example, your weekly pay is $1,140, so your fortnightly gross is $2,280.

## The Role of Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a casual loading of 25% on top of your base hourly rate. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave, public holidays, or other entitlements that permanent employees get. The casual loading is added to your base rate before any calculations.

For instance, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. With casual loading, it becomes $33.05 per hour. When converting to annual pay, use the loaded rate. For 38 hours per week, that is $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80 gross per year.

It is important to note that award rates may differ from the minimum wage. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Ombudsman for specific industries and occupations. They often include higher base rates or additional penalties. Casual loading is applied on top of the award rate unless the award specifies a loaded all-inclusive rate. Always check your award or agreement. Our [pay guides](/blog) can help you find the correct rate for your industry.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is a compulsory contribution your employer makes into a super fund on your behalf. The Super Guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your salary. This means your total remuneration package includes your gross pay plus super.

Using the $30 per hour example, your annual gross is $59,280. Your employer must contribute 12% of that, which is $7,113.60, into your super fund. Your total package is $66,393.60. The super contribution is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year, so if your earnings exceed that, the employer only pays super on the first $270,830.

Super is not deducted from your hourly rate; it is an additional cost for the employer. When comparing job offers, always consider the total package including super. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Salary Sacrifice and Airport Lounge Membership

Salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you agree to receive a lower gross salary in exchange for a non-cash benefit provided by your employer. Common benefits include cars, laptops, and even airport lounge memberships. A salary sacrifice airport lounge membership can be a tax-effective way to enjoy travel perks, as the cost is taken from your pre-tax income.

How does this affect your pay calculation? If you sacrifice part of your salary for a benefit, your taxable income decreases, which may reduce the tax you pay. However, your super guarantee may also be affected because super is calculated on your ordinary time earnings, which can be reduced by certain salary sacrifice arrangements. For example, if you sacrifice $2,000 per year for an airport lounge membership, your ordinary earnings for super purposes might drop to $57,280 (from $59,280), meaning your employer's super contribution would be 12% of $57,280 = $6,873.60 instead of $7,113.60.

It is essential to understand the rules. The Australian Taxation Office provides guidance on what counts as ordinary earnings. Salary sacrifice into super is treated differently from sacrifice for other benefits. Always consult your employer or a tax professional before entering into a salary sacrifice arrangement.

## Tax and Medicare

Once you have your gross annual pay, you need to estimate tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income, with reductions available for low-income earners. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. This is an estimate only. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more personalised calculation.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) is the simplest way to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Enter your base hourly rate, and if you are casual, check the box to add 25% casual loading. The tool automatically calculates gross pay, super, and estimated tax. It assumes 38 hours per week and the same rate every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Salary sacrifice is not included, so adjust manually if needed.

Remember that this is an estimate. Your actual pay may vary based on your award, agreement, and individual circumstances. Always refer to official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office for definitive information.
